title: Evaluation of ChatGPT and Microsoft Bing AI Chat Performances on Physics Exams of Vietnamese National High School Graduation Examination
extended_summary:
This paper evaluates how well two large language models, ChatGPT and Microsoft BingChat, answer physics questions taken from Vietnamese National High School Graduation Examination materials. The core question is whether these generative AI systems can perform at a level comparable to Vietnamese high school students on authentic exam items, especially across different difficulty levels from knowledge to high application.

The study uses the VNHSGE physics dataset, which contains multiple-choice questions from real Vietnamese national exams from 2019 to 2023. The authors compare the models’ answers with official solutions and with performance patterns from Vietnamese students. They also examine question difficulty, year-by-year performance, and a few illustrative examples of model outputs.

Overall, the paper finds that both ChatGPT and BingChat can answer easier questions reasonably well, but they struggle on more complex application and high-application problems. BingChat is generally more accurate, while ChatGPT is described as more stable or consistent. When compared with Vietnamese student score distributions, both models perform worse than students overall, leading the authors to conclude that current LLMs cannot yet replace human capability in high school physics teaching, though they may still be useful for immediate feedback and individualized support.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical benchmarking study, but it is not a controlled K-12 intervention trial; it evaluates model performance on exam items and compares against student score distributions. The methodology is systematic but observational and non-experimental, so it fits a lower-causal-strength evidence tier.
impact_tier_rationale: The study shows the models can solve some lower-level physics questions, but performance is below Vietnamese students on average and notably weak on higher-order application items. The practical impact for K-12 teaching is therefore promising but limited and not yet robust enough for strong positive classification.

interventions.use_case: Benchmarking ChatGPT and Microsoft BingChat on Vietnamese high school physics multiple-choice exam questions (2019-2023) to assess their potential as physics teaching and homework-support chatbots
Using ChatGPT and BingChat to translate and explain physics exam questions, and to provide immediate feedback and individualized learning support in K-12 physics contexts

finding.finding_summary: Across 200 exam questions from five Vietnamese high school physics exams, ChatGPT averaged 61% accuracy and BingChat 66%, both below Vietnamese students’ performance on the same exams (average student score 6.39/10; ChatGPT converted score 6.1; BingChat 6.6). The models handled knowledge and comprehension items reasonably well but struggled with high-application physics questions, indicating limited capability for complex scientific reasoning.
finding.measure: Accuracy on physics multiple-choice exam questions; converted exam scores compared with Vietnamese student score distributions

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT was more stable, while BingChat was more accurate on average across years. ChatGPT averaged 61% accuracy versus BingChat’s 66%, but the paper reports that ChatGPT was more consistent across years and question orders, whereas BingChat varied more substantially (e.g., 55% to 72.5% by year).
finding.measure: Year-by-year accuracy and response stability on physics exam questions

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that LLMs can support teachers and students by providing immediate feedback, individualized learning experiences, and assistance with lesson preparation and grading-related tasks. This is presented as a potential benefit rather than a directly measured experimental effect.
finding.measure: Proposed support for feedback, personalization, and teacher assistance
